excerpt: Mio connects Google Chat, Microsoft Teams and Slack so people on different chat platforms can message, share files and see each other's directories.
content:
Mio makes interoperability software for workplace chat. It relays messages in real time between Google Chat, Microsoft Teams and Slack, so a company that uses more than one platform, or works with partners on another one, can talk without everyone switching apps. Its products cover directory sync (so users can find each other across platforms), chat sync, external chat sync with other organisations, calendar sync and file sync. Its website names frontline workers, mergers and acquisitions, long-term coexistence of two platforms and avoiding vendor lock-in as the main uses.

According to its about page, Mio started in 2018, when large companies were increasingly using two or more messaging apps internally, and began with chat interoperability before adding identity management, file sharing and meeting features. It describes itself as a Google partner that works with the Google Workspace team on collaboration between Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams and Slack. Mio's site lists customer logos including large enterprises. We did not find recent independent press coverage of its funding, so this page sticks to what the company itself publishes.

Mio publishes how its pricing works but not the price per user. Only people who need cross-platform chat need a licence; licences are charged per user per month with a minimum one-year commitment, the price depends on which platforms are connected and how many users there are, and there is a flat one-time implementation fee of $10,000. It suits IT teams at companies running Google Workspace alongside Microsoft 365 or Slack, for example after a merger.

We have not used Mio for this page. It brings together Mio's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.

faq.a: It syncs messages, files, directories and calendars between Google Chat, Microsoft Teams and Slack.
Licences are priced per user per month with a one-year minimum, quoted on request, plus a $10,000 one-time implementation fee.
Its about page says it began in 2018.

faq.q: Do all employees need a Mio licence?
faq.a: No. Only users who need cross-platform chat need one, according to Mio's pricing page.
